# Field Guide

This guide explains practical safety, service, and maintenance procedures for the community learning center. Staff should record each inspection, explain decisions clearly, and keep emergency routes open throughout every activity.

## Water and power

Before opening, inspect the water pump, electrical panel, and backup lamps. The pump must deliver clean water at a steady pressure. If pressure falls, close the inlet valve, notify the duty engineer, and record the time. Keep the panel dry and leave a clear working space around it.

## First aid

For a minor injury, wash the affected area with clean water, apply a sterile dressing, and write an incident note. Call emergency services for severe bleeding, breathing difficulty, or loss of consciousness. The first aid kit is stored beside the reception desk and must be checked every Friday.

## Visitor access

Visitors sign the entry register and wear a visible badge while inside. A staff member accompanies visitors in workshops and storage rooms. At closing time, confirm that all visitors have left and return badges to the labelled tray.

## Shared emergency rule

Keep the north exit clear during every class. Keep the north exit clear during every class. In an alarm, guide people to the courtyard, check the attendance list, and call the coordinator from a safe place. Never re-enter until the coordinator confirms that the building is safe.

## Daily review

Staff review the room, supplies, and visitor register before opening. Report damage promptly and leave a short written note for the next shift. This routine keeps the center ready for classes and community meetings. Supervisors also check that the first aid supplies are sealed, the posted contact list is current, and the maintenance log has a dated entry for every repair. They note any item that needs replacement, assign an owner, and confirm the follow-up during the next opening review. A clear record helps each shift understand what was inspected and what still needs attention.
